target_customer: Mobile gamers who wanted physical buttons on a smartphone
problem: Touchscreens give no tactile feedback, which makes many mobile games hard to control.

founders.name: Connor Zwick
founders.background_notes: YC bio: sold previous company Flashcards+ to Chegg.

founders.name: Colton Gyulay
founders.background_notes: YC page lists as founder with no bio.

competitors.name: iCade Mobile (Ion Audio)
competitors.what: Cradle with D-pad and buttons for iPhone and iPod touch
competitors.traction_then: Shown at CES 2012; planned 2012 price 79.99 dollars

competitors.name: Gametel
competitors.what: Console style game controller for Android phones
competitors.traction_then: Shown at CES 2012, on sale for some time on Android

technical_complexity.rationale: Consumer hardware with a headphone jack interface needed industrial design, manufacturing and game support for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Accessory controllers were already shipping, and game support depended on developers adopting the input.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found on incumbent action against Coco; iCade-style rivals already shipped in 2012.

market_need_then: Mobile gaming was growing and several accessory makers showed controllers at CES 2012, indicating demand for physical controls.

branding.domain_note: Website listed as milkshakelabs.com, which now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page.
branding.community_and_virality: Design Boom ran a piece describing Coco as a smartphone case that doubles as a controller, connecting through the headphone jack.

brand_strength.rationale: A single design blog item was found; no community, merch or lasting identity, and many unrelated companies share the name.

outcome_analysis: Coco Controller was a two founder hardware startup in YC Summer 2012 building a tactile controller case for phones, led by a founder who had sold a prior app to Chegg. Rivals such as iCade Mobile and Gametel were already shown at CES in January 2012. The cause of inactivity is not public, and no source gives a shutdown date, so failure factors are recorded only as other.
notes: milkshakelabs.com redirects to a domain sale page, so the site is dead. The 125K seed rests on a single database (Dealroom, labeled AI generated) and Crunchbase shows a seed with Y Combinator and hidden amounts; it may be the standard YC deal. Dealroom also says both founders were Harvard dropouts, which is not confirmed by an opened primary source so education is left empty. One search summary named only Gyulay as founder; the YC page opened lists both. I could not open the designboom page, only its search listing.
